# Account Lifecycle & State Checklist: Accounts and invitations

**Purpose**: Validate that the requirements governing how an account comes into being, is closed, and is reopened are complete, consistent and objectively verifiable
**Created**: 2026-08-30
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.
**Coverage pass, 2026-08-31**: every item was re-read against `spec.md`, `plan.md`, `research.md`, `data-model.md`, `contracts/`, entry R1's and R2's artifacts, `docs/product/specifications.md` and `AGENTS.md`. Items marked **Covered** were already answered by one of those, and each names where — so a criterion satisfied by a design artifact rather than by `spec.md` is visible as such. Items marked **Resolved** were answered by amending `spec.md` in the same pass, and name the requirement that now carries them.

**Scope note**: This entry makes several strong negative claims — nothing is removed, nothing is recorded, nobody is notified, nothing is left for the account holder to do. A negative claim is only testable if what it excludes is enumerated, which is what most of the items below examine.

## Coming into being

- [x] CHK001 Are the two routes into existence stated in a way that makes SC-002 checkable? [Measurability, Spec §FR-035, §SC-002] — SC-002 claims 100% of accounts originate from an invitation or the seed; verify the requirement enumerates the exclusions rather than asserting the total. → **Covered**: `data-model.md` §2 and §5 — `user` is inserted by acceptance alone, seeding is R1's, and the four public routes are enumerated in `contracts/invitations.md` and `contracts/accounts-screen.md`.
- [x] CHK002 Is the joined date's definition unambiguous for both origins? [Clarity, Spec §FR-041] — "the instant the account came into being" is stated for acceptance; the seeded first admin's is not separately addressed. → **Covered**: `data-model.md`'s `AccountRow` — `joinedAt` is `user.created_at`, one definition covering both origins.
- [x] CHK003 Are the field-level requirements for the acceptance form complete? [Completeness, Spec §FR-026] — first name, last name and password are named; whether either name may be empty, its length bound, and how it is trimmed are not. → **Covered**: `contracts/server-mutators.md` — `firstName`, `lastName` and `password`, trimmed and bounded at §5's 200; `AcceptState`'s `names` covers an empty one.
- [x] CHK004 Is the created account's address required to match the invitation's exactly, including case folding? [Clarity, Spec §FR-028, §FR-010] — FR-010 fixes comparison folding; the *stored* form of the new account's address is not stated. → **Covered**: `contracts/server-mutators.md` *Case folding happens once* — `parseEmail` lower-cases on the way in, and the stored address is the invitation's.
- [x] CHK005 Is the must-change-password exclusion stated as a property of the created account rather than of the form? [Clarity, Spec §FR-030] → **Covered**: `contracts/server-mutators.md` writes `must_change_password: false` on the row, and `contracts/invitations.md` restates it as a property of the account rather than of the form.
- [x] CHK006 Are requirements defined for what the person sees between submitting acceptance and landing on `/home`? [Coverage, Spec §FR-028] — this is the one write in the feature that both creates and authenticates. → **Resolved**: `FR-028a` — the acceptance control shows in-flight state and takes no second press while the write is outstanding.

## Closing

- [x] CHK007 Is FR-047's "MUST remove nothing" enumerated well enough to be verified? [Measurability, Spec §FR-047] — memberships, assignments, comments and activity are named; verify the list is closed rather than illustrative. → **Covered**: `data-model.md` §2 *What it does not write* and §5's read-boundary table close the list: `deactivated_at` and the session rows are everything deactivation touches.
- [x] CHK008 Do FR-047 and FR-048 agree about where a closed account's name appears? [Conflict, Spec §FR-047, §FR-048] — FR-047 requires the name still render "everywhere it already did"; FR-048 requires exclusion from every picker. Whether an existing assignment shown inside a picker is covered by one or the other is not resolved. → **Covered**: `docs/product/specifications.md` §3.9 with §3.5 and §3.7 — a picker's candidate **pool** excludes deactivated users, while a value already set still renders under their name.
- [x] CHK009 Is self-closure stated as a requirement rather than only as an edge case? [Gap, Spec Edge Cases] — the *Edge Cases* section permits an admin to close their own account where they are not the last; no numbered requirement says so. → **Covered**: `contracts/server-mutators.md` — "An admin may close their own account where they are not the last active one — the count is the only guard the source states."
- [x] CHK010 Are requirements defined for what the acting admin experiences when they close their own account? [Gap, Spec §FR-045, Edge Cases] — their own session is deleted by the write they are awaiting, so the response to that request has no stated behaviour. → **Covered**: `contracts/server-mutators.md` and spec *Edge Cases* — their own sessions go with the rest, so their next request redirects to `/signin`.
- [x] CHK011 Is the closure instant required to be recorded, and is that consistent with FR-053? [Consistency, Spec §FR-045, §FR-053, Key Entities] — Key Entities calls closure "a deactivation instant" while FR-053 forbids retaining history; verify the instant is state rather than history under the spec's own definition. → **Covered**: `data-model.md` §2 — `deactivated_at` is the whole of it, so the instant is the state; no history and no acting admin is kept.
- [x] CHK012 Is FR-052's "notify nobody" verifiable given no notification system exists yet? [Measurability, Spec §FR-052] — entry R11 delivers notifications; state what this requirement asserts in the meantime. → **Covered**: `data-model.md` §2 — neither an `activity` row nor a `notification` row is written, which is falsifiable by row count against tables that already exist in §5.
- [x] CHK013 Are requirements defined for outstanding invitations issued *by* an account that is then closed? [Coverage, Spec §FR-018, Edge Cases] — the edge case confirms the name still renders in the "invited by" column; whether those invitations remain live and resendable is not stated. → **Covered**: `data-model.md`'s `InvitationRow` and `research.md` A-6 — the cascade never fires, the inviter's name renders like any other, and `resendInvite`'s only refusal is a missing row.
- [x] CHK014 Is the closed-account sign-in message's ownership stated, so a reviewer knows whether its wording is fixed here or inherited? [Traceability, Spec §FR-046] → **Covered**: `research.md` C-5 — the wording is R1's, asserted against its existing `{ result: "deactivated", contact }` response rather than restated here.

## Reopening

- [x] CHK015 Does SC-009's "nothing for the account holder to do" hold given FR-045 deleted every session? [Conflict, Spec §SC-009, §FR-045, §FR-051] — a reopened account's holder must sign in again, which is something to do. Verify the success criterion means no *credential or invitation* step, and says so. → **Resolved**: `SC-009` now reads "no step asked of the account holder beyond signing in with the password they already had", and `FR-051a` states that deleted sessions do not come back.
- [x] CHK016 Is FR-051's "restore the memberships it already had" accurate given FR-047 removed nothing? [Clarity, Spec §FR-051, §FR-047] — as written it implies a restoration step that has nothing to restore; an implementer may add one. → **Covered**: `contracts/server-mutators.md` — "Memberships are untouched because none are read or written"; `data-model.md` shows `deactivated_at = null` as the only write.
- [x] CHK017 Can SC-009's "restores exactly what it had" be objectively verified? [Measurability, Spec §SC-009] — the comparison needs a stated set of properties to hold constant. → **Covered**: `data-model.md` §2 — closure writes one column and deletes session rows, so the property set reopening must restore is closed and comparable.
- [x] CHK018 Are requirements defined for whether reactivation is offered on an account closed by the command line rather than this screen? [Coverage, Spec §FR-042, §FR-051] — R1's `admin:deactivate` produces the same state; verify the roster's control is defined by state rather than by origin. → **Covered**: `data-model.md`'s `isActive` and `contracts/accounts-screen.md`'s control cell define the control by state, never by origin.
- [x] CHK019 Is the reactivated account's role stated? [Gap, Spec §FR-051] — the role is untouched by closure, but FR-029 fixes a role at creation only, and no requirement says closure and reopening leave it alone. → **Covered**: `contracts/server-mutators.md` — `reactivateUser`'s only write is `deactivated_at = null`, so the role is untouched by both transitions.

## The closed account's remaining surface

- [x] CHK020 Are requirements defined for a closed account that receives a fresh invitation attempt through the mutator rather than the form? [Gap, Spec §FR-008a] — FR-008a fixes the *inline* refusal and offers Reactivate; no requirement bars `inviteUser` from writing an invitation for that address. → **Covered**: `contracts/server-mutators.md` — `inviteUser`'s *Refuses* row carries `has_account`, which `AddressCheck` marks `isDeactivated`; the mutator refuses, not only the field.
- [x] CHK021 Is the claim that a closed account cannot hold an outstanding invitation derivable from the requirements? [Traceability, Spec Edge Cases] — the edge case asserts it follows from ordering; verify no path (acceptance then closure then re-invitation) reaches that state. → **Covered**: With that mutator refusal and `data-model.md`'s lifecycle (SPENT is never listed), no path reaches a closed account holding an outstanding invitation.
- [x] CHK022 Are requirements defined for the closed account's own profile and password-change surfaces? [Coverage, Spec §FR-045] — entry R4 owns the profile screen; the interaction with closure is created here. → **Covered**: R1 `FR-021` — a session whose user is deactivated resolves to no actor, closing every authenticated surface; R1's edge case covers the reset.
- [x] CHK023 Is the roster's treatment of a closed account's project count specified? [Coverage, Spec §FR-040] — the count reads zero for everyone until R5; whether closure changes it afterwards is not stated. → **Covered**: `data-model.md` and `contracts/accounts-screen.md` — `projectCount` is a literal `0` for every row until R5, closed or active alike.

## Population invariants

- [x] CHK024 Is the last-admin guard stated in terms of the resulting population rather than the operation? [Clarity, Spec §FR-049, §SC-008] — verify the requirement forbids the end state (zero active admins), which also covers routes other than deactivation. → **Covered**: `research.md` A-4 and `docs/product/specifications.md` §2 — the guard counts the active-admin population under a row lock, across demotion and deactivation alike.
- [x] CHK025 Are requirements defined for the interaction between closure and role change? [Gap, Spec §FR-049] — role changes are command-line only; demoting the last active admin reaches the same forbidden state by another path, and only the deactivation path is guarded here. → **Covered**: `docs/product/specifications.md` §2 — `setUserRole` and `deactivateUser` share the count and the lock; spec *Reconciliations* confirms the mechanism is R1's rather than a second one.
- [x] CHK026 Is the guard's scope stated as installation-wide? [Clarity, Spec §FR-049] — "the installation" is used; verify it is defined rather than assumed. → **Covered**: `research.md` A-4 selects the active admins with no narrower scope, and `plan.md`'s *Scale/Scope* fixes one installation.
- [x] CHK027 Are requirements defined for whether a closed admin still counts as an admin for any purpose? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-049, §FR-042] — the roster shows the role of closed accounts, and the guard counts only active ones. → **Covered**: The guard counts active admins only (`research.md` A-4), the roster shows a closed account's role (`data-model.md`), and `docs/product/specifications.md` §3.5/§3.7 exclude them from every pool.

## Ordering, presentation and scope

- [x] CHK028 Is the roster's two-group ordering required to update immediately after a state change? [Coverage, Spec §FR-036, §FR-056] — a deactivated account must move between groups; whether that is a re-query or an in-place move is not stated. → **Covered**: `research.md` C-4 and `contracts/ux-conventions.md` — every mutator ends with `revalidatePath`, so both groups re-render from a fresh query.
- [x] CHK029 Are the roster's columns specified completely enough to render a closed account? [Completeness, Spec §FR-037] — every column is defined for an active account; none is stated to differ or be absent when closed. → **Covered**: `data-model.md`'s `AccountRow` and `contracts/accounts-screen.md` define every cell without reference to state; only the control cell differs.
- [x] CHK030 Is the deferral of FR-048's picker exclusion stated so later entries can discharge it? [Traceability, Spec §FR-048] — the requirement is owed here but takes effect in R5, R6 and R7; verify what this feature must deliver for them is stated as a testable obligation. → **Covered**: `contracts/accounts-screen.md` — what this feature owes is that `deactivated_at` is set and every session is gone, which is precisely what the later exclusions read.
- [x] CHK031 Are the requirements consistent that no account is ever deleted? [Consistency, Spec §FR-047, Out of Scope, Key Entities] — three places assert it; verify none of the mutators specified here is permitted to contradict it. → **Covered**: `data-model.md` §2 and §5 with R1's `FR-007` — `user` is inserted and updated, never deleted, and no mutator here is permitted a delete.
- [x] CHK032 Is every claim in FR-052 and FR-053 paired with an acceptance scenario that could fail? [Traceability, Spec §FR-052, §FR-053] — story 4 scenarios 10 and 11 cover them; verify each negative claim is falsifiable as written. → **Covered**: `data-model.md` §2 enumerates the tables neither mutator writes, and the schema carries no history column, so both negative claims fail by row count.
